legend: You are on vacation in a foreign country. This country has a local football league, and you don't know any of the team names. However, you have found a table of all the results from this season, and next to every match is the concatenated names of the two teams that played.

There are n%%ZSMJ0%% teams in total, named s1,s2,⋯,sn%%ZSMJ1%%. You are given the concatenation si+sj%%ZSMJ2%% for every ordered pair i≠j%%ZSMJ3%%. Find the teams names s1,s2,⋯,sn%%ZSMJ4%%. Team names must be nonempty, but they do not need to be distinct.
input: The first line of input contains the integer n%%ZSMJ5%% (2≤n≤500%%ZSMJ6%%).

The following n%%ZSMJ7%% lines each contain n%%ZSMJ8%% strings, the table of concatenated team names. The j%%ZSMJ9%%:th string on the i%%ZSMJ10%%:th of these lines will contain the string si+sj%%ZSMJ11%% if i≠j%%ZSMJ12%%, and "*" if i=j%%ZSMJ13%%. The concatenated team names will consist of lower case characters a-z.
The total number of characters in concatenated team names is at most 106%%ZSMJ14%%.
output: If there is no solution, print "NONE".
If there is more than one solution, print "MANY".
If there is one unique solution, print "UNIQUE", followed by n%%ZSMJ15%% lines containing s1,s2,⋯,sn%%ZSMJ16%%.
